newsitem.title: USA: US excess aluminum capacity used up in 1998-Alumax.
newsitem.headline: US excess aluminum capacity used up in 1998-Alumax.

text.p: Excess aluminum production capacity in North America will be used up by the end of 1998, helped by the growing demand from the carmakers, Allen Born, Chief Executive of Alumax Inc, said.
Born predicted rising demand for aluminum from emerging markets and from auto makers whom, he said have finally been convinced of aluminum's structural and metallurgical superiority to steel.
Asked if demand from carmakers would be enough to absorb ideld North American capacity, he responded: "That capacity can probably be eaten up next year, to tell you the truth."
Asked if he expected idled capacity to be eaten in 1998, he replied: "I think so...by the end of next year."
Some 800,000 to one million tonnes of primary aluminum capacity remains idled in North America, largely at Alcoa, and Reynolds Metals, with some at Alcan's plants in the U.S. and Canada.
Born predicted that half of all U.S. made cars would be constructed entirely of aluminum within ten years, and said aluminum makers would begin to look for alliances with car manufacturers.
"Their demand will stabilise the market," the executive told a news conference at Alumitech, an industry forum organised by the Aluminum Association.
"(Auto) manufacturers have determined our metal is the metal they have to use in the next ten to fifteen years," Born said.

Earlier Born told delegates that by 2004 there will be a prototype vehicle available which can travel 80 miles per gallon and will be extremely aluminum intensive, the result of a partnership between the Big Three auto makers and government agencies, including NASA, the Department of Energy and Department of Defense.
